title: Resolve race condition causing parent-org billing tags to be attached after sub-account key swap
creator: Luis Ortega
description:
Observed a recurring class of misattributed usage where, immediately after a sub-account API key swap, a subset of requests are charged to the parent org instead of the sub-account. This manifests as short spikes of parent-tenant token usage in the billing pipeline and incorrect quota enforcement for the sub-account. Initial hypothesis: a race between the TokenRegistry update and the attribution cache invalidation combined with the rate-limiter keying logic which falls back to the parent org when the sub-account mapping is momentarily missing.

Reproduction notes:
- Steps: rotate a sub-account API key via /admin/keys/swap while concurrently sending streaming generation requests from the old client socket.
- Observed behavior: ~0.5-2% of requests in the 30s window after swap get attributed to parent org.
- Environment: reproduced in staging against a 3-node runtime cluster with sticky sessions enabled.

Evidence collected:
- Datadog graph: https://app.datadoghq.com/dashboard/ABC123/billing-anomalies shows parent-usage spikes aligned to swap events.
- Logs: attribution-service TRACE shows TTL cache miss for mapping key -> subaccount_id followed by fallback path logline "no-subaccount-mapping, using parent org".
- SQL sample that surfaced the stale mapping: SELECT tenant_id, api_key_id, updated_at FROM api_key_mappings WHERE api_key_id = '<rotated_key>' ORDER BY updated_at DESC; returned old mapping record that had been soft-deleted but still present in in-memory cache.
- Rate limiter behaviour: limiter key uses (tenant_id || workspace_id) resolved from attribution service. When mapping miss occurs, code path emits a fallback owner_id which becomes parent org id.

Initial impact: billing spikes for ~10 orgs in last 30 days; at least 3 customers reported quota overages. We believe this is primarily a correctness/regression issue (not fraud).

Work to do (high level):
1) Add a short-term mitigation to attribution-service: treat soft-deleted mappings as authoritative for a configurable grace window rather than returning nothing.
2) Add distributed lock or atomic swap in TokenRegistry so key rotation is visible to all attribution nodes before old mapping is invalidated.
3) Change rate-limiter to not fall back to parent org when mapping is unknown; instead reject with a 401/429 that surfaces the 'mapping-missing' code and increments a monitoring counter.
4) Backfill/repair: identify affected windows and run backfill to move misattributed token usage to correct sub-accounts for billing reconciliation.
5) Add unit + integration tests and a canary rollout strategy with a traffic shadow for 24 hours.

Acceptance criteria:
- No parent-org usage spikes in staging during key rotation tests.
- New telemetry covers mapping-miss occurrences and fallback rejections.
- Backfill script validated and run for impacted customers.
comments: 2026-02-28 - Luis Ortega: Created ticket after morning incident post key-swap in staging; filed Datadog dashboard and collected log traces. Marking as P0 due to customer quota impact.
2026-03-01 - Aisha Patel: Reproduced locally on staging. Confirmed TTL-based cache miss is frequent when swaps are processed on different nodes. Attached sample logs and SQL extract to the ticket.

2026-03-03 - Michael Tan (SRE): Observed sticky-session behaviour prolongs the window where old workers route to nodes without updated mappings. Proposed short-term fix: propagate mapping writes via the gossip bus with sequence numbers.

2026-03-05 - Aisha Patel: Implemented a prototype change (branch: feat/atomic-key-swap) that writes mapping and a sequence token. Attribution nodes now compare sequence token before serving mapping. Benchmarked in staging: median attribution latency +2ms, tail unchanged.

2026-03-08 - QA: Running integration job that exercises 10k key-swaps with sustained traffic. Found an edge case when a node restarts during the swap window and lease refresh delays mapping propagation. Added restart handling to prototype.

2026-03-10 - Aisha Patel: Prepared rollout plan: canary to 5% runtime traffic for 24h -> 25% -> 100% if no mapping-miss alerts. Backfill script draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/billing/pull/487.
next_steps: Finish atomic swap prototype, add mapping-miss rejection and telemetry, run backfill test in staging, then perform staged canary rollout. Coordinate with support for customer communications and billing corrections.
owner_notes: Prioritize telemetry so we can quantify fix effectiveness. If the sequence-token approach causes unexpected load, fall back to conservative TTL extension for soft-deletes and re-evaluate.
